correctness.rationale: An exact arch-structure theorem reduces every shortest ternary k-universal word to k concatenated permutations. A length-three forbidden factor crosses at most one such block boundary. The six-state transfer matrices in RESULT.md are therefore exact for every integer k>=1. Determinant identities of explicit integer-polynomial matrices produce the four claimed rational functions, and the primitive transition graphs yield distinct growth constants. The provided standard-library verifier replays all four exact determinant identities and 20,439 independent direct word checks; finite counts are not substituted for the transfer proof.

Generic regular-language counting algorithms compute terms but do not state the four closed rational functions; two numerical sequences are already present in OEIS, limiting the claim to their combined word-theoretic interpretation and the full four-type growth classification.
residual_risks: A regular-language counting theorem includes an algorithm that can compute every coefficient, so the contribution is limited to closed forms and complete special classification.

A specialized formula in unindexed literature or an algebraically equivalent formulation could remain undiscovered.

value.rationale: An exhaustive symmetry classification of all 27 length-three forbidden factors in the smallest genuinely nonbinary alphabet is natural rather than an arbitrary pattern slice. The exact infinite-k rational generating functions divide them into four unequal exponential-growth types and provide exact benchmarks for constrained-subsequence-universality counting. The asymptotic distinctions and all-pattern coverage are more informative than a numerical census or an isolated transfer-matrix instance; the result does not claim a general-alphabet theorem.
